result: The Tsc2cKOPrrx1-cre mouse model was successfully generated with efficient Tsc2 disruption in mesenchymal cells. PCR analysis showed nearly complete recombination in limb skin fibroblasts but not epidermal cells (C53-C54), Western blot demonstrated loss of Tsc2 protein and increased S6 phosphorylation indicating mTORC1 hyperactivation (C55-C56), and flow cytometry showed ~95% EYFP expression in cultured fibroblasts (C57).
evaluation: Multiple complementary techniques (PCR, Western blot, flow cytometry, fluorescence imaging) consistently demonstrate efficient and specific Tsc2 disruption in mesenchymal cells with expected downstream mTORC1 activation. The mesenchymal specificity is confirmed by absence of recombination in epidermal cells (C54). Sample sizes and technical replicates appear adequate based on figure legends.

result: Tsc2cKOPrrx1-cre mice exhibited multiple phenotypic abnormalities including skeletal changes (shorter/thicker extremities, thicker bones, bulbous snout; C58-C60), thickened hypercellular dermis (C61), and reduced survival with median of ~24 weeks without gender difference (C62-C63). Blood analysis at 17 weeks revealed anemia but normal kidney/liver function markers (C64-C65).
evaluation: The phenotypic characterization is comprehensive with multiple anatomical and physiological measurements. Survival analysis uses appropriate Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank test (C62-C63). The anemia finding (C64) may partially explain reduced survival, though the authors note this is not fully explained. Statistical significance is properly reported for dermal thickness (p<0.001, C61).

result: Tsc2cKOPrrx1-cre mice developed extensive vascular hamartomas in multiple organs. Serial MRI showed progressive development of kidney cysts (6/6 mice by 12 weeks), spleen enlargement (5/6 by 12 weeks), and subcutaneous fluid accumulation (C67-C69). Histological analysis revealed vascular anomalies with tortuous dilated vessels, abnormal smooth muscle, fragmented elastic fibers resembling human AML (C76-C77), and HMB-45 positive staining characteristic of LAM/AML (C87). EYFP expression was detected in vessel endothelial cells and perivascular cells (C83), and fluid analysis suggested chylous contribution (C89).
evaluation: The tumor characterization is thorough with longitudinal MRI tracking (n=6 mice), detailed histopathology, and multiple immunohistochemical markers. The presence of EYFP+ endothelial cells (C83) is unexpected given Prrx1-cre expression patterns but is well-documented with appropriate controls (C84). The similarity to human AML pathology (fragmented elastin, HMB-45 positivity) strengthens translational relevance. Sample sizes are adequate for pathological analysis (n=11 mice, Table 2).

result: Tumors contain both Tsc2-deficient mesenchymal and endothelial cells. PCR detected low levels of recombined Tsc2 allele in neonatal organs before tumor formation, with increased levels in adult tumors indicating KO cell expansion (C90-C91). Real-time PCR copy number analysis confirmed ~90% reduction in Tsc2 exon 3 in EYFP+ splenocytes (C92). Flow cytometry showed ~50% of cultured splenocytes expressed CD90.2 (mesenchymal marker), including most EYFP+ cells (C94), and paw tumor cells contained EYFP+ endothelial cells (C95) unlike control tissue (C96).
evaluation: The cellular composition analysis uses appropriate quantitative methods (real-time PCR, flow cytometry) with proper controls. The finding of EYFP+ endothelial cells in tumors but not controls (C95-C96) is well-documented and discussed as unexpected. The CD90.2 staining (C94) confirms mesenchymal identity. The progression from low neonatal to high adult Tsc2- allele levels (C90-C91) provides evidence for clonal expansion.

result: Sirolimus treatment blocked abnormalities in Tsc2cKOPrrx1-cre mice. Treatment from postnatal day 25 for 30 days significantly reduced forepaw thickness (C97) and dermal thickness by 35% (C98, p=0.003). Post-treatment analysis showed forepaw hamartomas in 8/8 vehicle-treated versus 1/10 sirolimus-treated mice (C99), with similar responses in kidney and spleen tumors (C100).
evaluation: The sirolimus experiment includes appropriate vehicle controls, adequate sample sizes (n=8-10 per group), proper statistical analysis (mixed model for repeated measures with Bonferroni correction), and significant p-values (p<0.001 for forepaw thickness at day 30, p=0.003 for dermal thickness). The dramatic reduction in tumor incidence (8/8 to 1/10) demonstrates strong mTORC1 dependence. This validates the model and confirms mTORC1 as the key driver.

result: RNA sequencing identified a Tsc2/mTORC1 expression signature in Tsc2-deficient fibroblasts that is enriched in human bladder cancers with TSC1/TSC2 mutations. Comparing KO versus WT fibroblasts revealed 1387 overexpressed and 437 underexpressed genes (FDR<10%; C101-C102), enriched for glucose metabolism, cell cycle, and HIF1α responses (C103). Sirolimus treatment affected more genes in KO (7282 under-, 2567 overexpressed) than WT cells (C104-C105), with 92% of KO-overexpressed genes corrected by sirolimus (C107). This signature showed higher scores in TSC1/TSC2 mutant bladder tumors (n=43) versus wildtype (n=348) in TCGA data (p=0.005; C110), and LGALS3 was specifically elevated in mutant tumors (p=0.015; C111).
evaluation: The transcriptomic analysis uses appropriate methods (RNA-seq with n=3 biological replicates per condition, FDR correction for multiple testing). The sirolimus correction of 92% of dysregulated genes (C107) validates mTORC1 dependence. Translation to human cancer using TCGA data (n=391 tumors) with significant p-values (p=0.005 for signature, p=0.015 for LGALS3) is well-executed. However, the signature's specificity to TSC1/TSC2 mutations versus other mTORC1-activating mutations is not tested, and validation in independent cohorts would strengthen the finding.

result: Galectin-3 is elevated in Tsc2-deficient mouse cells and tissues. Lgals3 expression was higher in KO versus WT fibroblasts (p=0.007) and corrected by sirolimus (C109). Immunohistochemistry showed dense Gal-3 positivity in vascular/perivascular cells of forelimb tumors (C113) and increased dermal fibroblasts (C115) compared to controls. In cultured KO fibroblasts, both intracellular and secreted Gal-3 were sharply increased and partially normalized by 48hr sirolimus treatment (C116-C117). Serum Gal-3 levels were 67% higher in adult Tsc2cKOPrrx1-cre mice (p=0.015; C118) and decreased 25% with sirolimus treatment (p=0.036; C119).
evaluation: Multiple complementary approaches (RNA-seq, IHC, Western blot, ELISA) consistently demonstrate Gal-3 elevation in Tsc2-deficient contexts. Statistical significance is reported for key comparisons with appropriate p-values. The partial normalization by sirolimus (C117, C119) confirms mTORC1 regulation. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=11-15 for serum measurements). The consistency across multiple assays and the dose-response to sirolimus strengthen confidence in this finding.

result: Galectin-3 is elevated in human TSC-related tumors. IHC showed abundant Gal-3+ dermal fibroblasts in TSC skin tumors versus minimal staining in normal-appearing skin (C120-C121). Fibroblasts from TSC skin tumors secreted more Gal-3 than normal skin fibroblasts (C122, p<0.05 for multiple tumor types), and Western blot confirmed higher intracellular Gal-3 in tumor versus paired normal fibroblasts from 4 patients (C123). Gal-3 expression was also observed in LAM lung nodules (C124) and renal angiomyolipomas (C125).
evaluation: The human tissue analysis includes multiple TSC manifestations (skin tumors n=4 types, LAM n=4, AML n=3) with appropriate normal controls. Statistical significance is reported for secreted Gal-3 (p=0.020-0.028 for different tumor types). The use of paired normal/tumor samples from the same patients (C123) controls for inter-individual variation. However, sample sizes are modest, and the Western blot shows variable Gal-3 levels among patients, suggesting heterogeneity that warrants larger validation studies.

result: Serum galectin-3 levels correlate with disease severity in LAM patients not taking mTOR inhibitors. In treatment-naïve LAM patients (n=64), %FEV1 negatively correlated with Gal-3 levels (r=-0.32, p=0.010; C126), and this remained significant after adjusting for BMI (partial r=-0.366, p=0.004; C130). No correlation was found in patients on mTOR inhibitors (n=72; C127). Two-way ANOVA showed Gal-3 levels were higher in mild LAM patients with AML versus without AML (p=0.045; C128). However, Gal-3 levels in LAM patients overall did not differ from normal subjects (C131).
evaluation: The correlation analysis includes adequate sample sizes (n=64 treatment-naïve, n=72 on mTOR inhibitors) and appropriate statistical methods (Pearson correlation, partial correlation adjusting for BMI, two-way ANOVA). The negative correlation with lung function (C126, C130) and positive association with AML in mild LAM (C128) are statistically significant. However, the lack of difference between LAM patients and normal subjects (C131) undermines the biomarker utility. The correlation is modest (r=-0.32) and the authors acknowledge that baseline differences in Gal-3 production and LGALS3 polymorphisms may confound interpretation. The study is also limited by its cross-sectional design—longitudinal data would be needed to establish Gal-3 as a prognostic marker.
